tasks.short: Interpret maintenance specifications to determine repair feasibility and method

steps.what: Locate applicable maintenance manuals, service bulletins and specifications
Read and interpret specifications to determine repair feasibility and the permitted method

tasks.design: Configure native component links to controlled specifications in {DOCS}. The mechanic verifies applicability and reads the complete instructions before determining feasibility and method.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the applicable current revision can require repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Document indexes can reuse checked component identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Damage limits and aircraft configuration require technical interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic connects approved instructions to actual component condition.
tasks.altitude: Less lookup; technical decision rights remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Controlled document links can reduce navigation without replacing technical interpretation; savings are an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is retrieval and interpretation, excluding repair execution and engineering approval.

Configuration control supplies existing aircraft identity, component part and serial number and modification status. Document control supplies revision and applicability through unchanged work. Test native indexing first; all85 interpretation hours remain. Existing automatic retrieval earns no saving.

tasks.short: Maintain preventive and corrective aircraft repair logs

steps.what: Capture performed maintenance, task references, parts and factual completion details
Transfer verified maintenance facts into the repair log
Verify completeness and record the accepted repair log entry

tasks.design: Capture maintenance facts once on a digital task card in {OPS_SYSTEM} and populate the repair-log draft from that record. The mechanic checks and accepts the complete entry; separate release-to-service certification retains its authorised process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper task-card facts may be retyped into repair logs.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital job cards and electronic technical logs support maintenance records.
tasks.still_hard: Actual work, parts identity and completion details must be accurate.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic verifies that the record reflects work actually performed.
tasks.altitude: Less transcription; certification and release rights remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: AMOS provides digital job cards and electronic signatures.
TrustFlight Tech Log replaces a paper aircraft technical log.
The transcription saving is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is mechanic record capture, transfer and acceptance, excluding maintenance execution and separate release-to-service certification.

Mechanic produces aircraft and task identity, work performed, date, parts and serials when relevant, test result and completion status in s1's45 hours. Digital capture retains that full time. Missing details require manual clarification; no automatic completion flag is inferred.
Test approved native records functionality first and follow local access and approval requirements. Already digital logs have no duplicate-transcription saving.
research_questions: Can one-time capture remove transcription while preserving complete traceability?

tasks.short: Interpret pilots' descriptions to diagnose problem causes

steps.what: Read pilots' descriptions, clarify symptoms and diagnose likely causes against aircraft context

tasks.design: Retain interpretation and diagnosis using the original report in {OPS_SYSTEM}. No shortened model summary replaces uncertain operating detail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reported symptoms can have several technical causes.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's record tools do not establish diagnosis automation.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a pilot's experience from a confirmed fault.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic asks precise questions and tests hypotheses.
tasks.altitude: No diagnostic time or authority change.

evidence.claim: Pilot-report interpretation remains technical judgement in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is report interpretation and diagnosis, excluding physical testing and log entry.
Pilot produces the original description through unchanged reporting work. Mechanic clarifies conditions within s1's100 hours; no structured fault code is assumed.
No new tool or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: What operating details must diagnostic reading preserve?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; all diagnostic reading remains.

tasks.short: Listen to engines to detect and diagnose malfunctions

steps.what: Listen to operating engines under authorised test conditions
Interpret sounds to detect and diagnose valve or other engine malfunctions

tasks.design: Retain authorised engine listening and interpretation with the mechanic. Existing procedures in {DOCS} guide tests; the digest supplies no validated acoustic classification change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sounds depend on operating conditions and mechanical context.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change replaces trained auditory inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Similar sounds can have different causes.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic links sounds to conditions and seeks confirming tests.
tasks.altitude: No listening or diagnosis time change.

evidence.claim: Trained engine listening and diagnosis remain human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is listening and interpretation, excluding repairs and other tests.
Mechanic produces sound observations in s1's45 hours and interprets them in s2's55 hours. No structured sound label or validated sensor feed is assumed.
No new tool or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
